+# Cospherical anchors and their common unit locus
+
+## Abstract
+
+The exact common unit-distance locus of a nonempty cospherical anchor family.
+
+This is the classical orthogonal decomposition of a sphere intersection. Orthogonal projection and subspace operations are reused from Mathlib. The anchor family is indexed by an arbitrary type with a chosen index; it need not be injective or finite. The ambient real inner product space is finite-dimensional.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Anchor affine direction).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Geometry/CosphericalUnitLocus.anchorDirection`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Geometry/CosphericalUnitLocus.anchorDirection` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The direction is the linear span of all differences x(i)-x(i0) from the chosen base anchor.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Constructed affine center).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Geometry/CosphericalUnitLocus.anchorCenter`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Geometry/CosphericalUnitLocus.anchorCenter` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Subtract from the base anchor its orthogonal projection onto the anchor direction. The result c is perpendicular to that direction and every anchor minus c lies in it.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (Exact unit-locus equivalence).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Geometry/CosphericalUnitLocus.common_unit_locus_iff`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Geometry/CosphericalUnitLocus.common_unit_locus_iff` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every real r, every anchor family x all of whose points have norm r, every chosen base index i0 and every ambient point p, all distances from p to the anchors equal one if and only if p-c belongs to the orthogonal complement of the anchor direction and norm(p-c) squared equals one minus r squared plus norm(c) squared. Both directions are proved for the same point p. Subtracting the squared distance equations establishes perpendicularity to every anchor difference, and orthogonal decomposition supplies the remaining scalar equation. The statement includes empty intersections and codimension-one two-point intersections. It does not itself assert nonemptiness, positive dimension, finite avoidance or a graph embedding.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (Faithful choices from a common-unit locus).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Geometry/CosphericalUnitLocus.exists_common_unit_avoiding`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Geometry/CosphericalUnitLocus.exists_common_unit_avoiding` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Assume the common anchor norm r is nonnegative and less than one, and the orthogonal complement of the anchor direction has dimension at least two. Every ambient-open patch containing a common-unit point contains one that avoids unit distance to a prescribed finite family of forbidden centers and avoids every point in a second finite family. Each forbidden center z must have norm different from r or lie outside the anchor affine hull, expressed as z-c not belonging to the anchor direction. If its restricted normal vanished and its unit sphere contained the allowed sphere, orthogonal decomposition would force both affine-hull membership and norm r, contradicting this hypothesis. The positive radius is constructed as the square root of one minus r squared plus norm(c) squared. The proved affine-sphere avoidance theorem then makes all finite choices simultaneously. No graph-level claim or arbitrary partial-placement extension follows without its additional geometric and combinatorial hypotheses.
+
+## References
+
+- Truth anchor: `D5/S3/Geometry/CosphericalUnitLocus.anchorCenter`
+- Truth anchor: `D5/S3/Geometry/CosphericalUnitLocus.anchorDirection`
+- Truth anchor: `D5/S3/Geometry/CosphericalUnitLocus.common_unit_locus_iff`
+- Truth anchor: `D5/S3/Geometry/CosphericalUnitLocus.exists_common_unit_avoiding`
+- Dependency: [D5/S3/Geometry/SphereSectionAvoidance](SphereSectionAvoidance.md)

+# Affine general position on a sphere
+
+## Abstract
+
+Finite affine-general-position configurations on positive-radius round spheres.
+
+These are classical general-position constructions. The proper-affine-span dimension bound and the affine-independence insertion criterion are reused from Mathlib; selection on the sphere uses the rational-circle finite-avoidance construction. No literature priority or graph-level realization result is asserted.
+
+**Theorem 1.1 (Joint avoidance of proper affine subspaces).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Geometry/SphereGeneralPosition.exists_on_sphere_avoiding_affine_subspaces`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Geometry/SphereGeneralPosition.exists_on_sphere_avoiding_affine_subspaces` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+In any finite-dimensional real inner product space of dimension at least two, every ambient-open patch meeting a positive-radius sphere has a point outside each member of any specified finite family of proper affine subspaces. Empty affine subspaces need no exclusion. For a nonempty proper affine subspace, its direction is proper and has a nonzero perpendicular normal. A fixed point determines its affine offset, so the sphere-section avoidance theorem applies.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Every finite cardinality in affine general position).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Geometry/SphereGeneralPosition.exists_sphere_general_position`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Geometry/SphereGeneralPosition.exists_sphere_general_position` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For every natural n and every positive real r there is a finite set s of cardinality n on the norm-r sphere such that every subset t of s with at most dim(E)+1 elements is affinely independent. The ambient finite-dimensional real inner product space E has dimension at least two. At each finite induction step the new point avoids the affine span of every old subset of size at most dim(E). These are proper affine subspaces by the cardinality bound. Avoiding singleton spans prevents collisions; the insertion criterion establishes independence for every newly formed subset. The case n=0 is included. For a three-dimensional carrier this gives any finite number of points on a two-sphere with every four independent; a four-dimensional carrier gives points on a three-sphere with every five independent.
+
+## References
+
+- Truth anchor: `D5/S3/Geometry/SphereGeneralPosition.exists_on_sphere_avoiding_affine_subspaces`
+- Truth anchor: `D5/S3/Geometry/SphereGeneralPosition.exists_sphere_general_position`

+# Finite avoidance on round spheres
+
+## Abstract
+
+Finite affine-section and collision avoidance in open patches of round spheres.
+
+The construction uses classical rational circle coordinates, finite unions of proper linear kernels and finiteness of the roots of a nonzero polynomial. The finite-union and root-finiteness results are reused from Mathlib. The carrier dimension is at least two and the radius is positive. Two-point spheres are outside these avoidance statements.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (Rational circle coordinates).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Geometry/SphereSectionAvoidance.circleArc`
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S3/Geometry/SphereSectionAvoidance.circleArc` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+For vectors x and v and real t, the arc is ((1-t squared)/(1+t squared)) times x plus (2t/(1+t squared)) times v. If x and v are perpendicular and have the same positive norm, every point of the arc has that norm. The parameter zero gives x.
+
+**Theorem 1.2 (Every nonempty open patch avoids finitely many affine hyperplanes).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Geometry/SphereSectionAvoidance.exists_on_sphere_avoiding_sections`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Geometry/SphereSectionAvoidance.exists_on_sphere_avoiding_sections` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner product space of dimension at least two, let r be positive, and let U be ambient-open with a point of norm r. For any finite family of nonzero normals a and arbitrary real offsets b, there is a point y in U of norm r with inner product of a(i) and y different from b(i) for every index. A tangent direction is selected to avoid all homogeneous sections passing through the starting point. Each remaining forbidden equation pulls back to a nonzero polynomial of degree at most two. A small interval of parameters stays in U and misses their finite root union.
+
+**Theorem 1.3 (Unit spheres and collisions in an actual affine carrier).**
+
+Lean statement: `D5/S3/Geometry/SphereSectionAvoidance.exists_on_affine_sphere_avoiding`
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S3/Geometry/SphereSectionAvoidance.exists_on_affine_sphere_avoiding` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let K be a linear subspace of a finite-dimensional real inner product space, with dimension at least two, c an arbitrary center and R a positive radius. Every ambient-open patch containing some c+w with w in K of norm R contains such a point avoiding finitely many unit spheres and finitely many specified collision points. For every unit-sphere center z, the precise properness hypothesis says that if the orthogonal projection of z-c into K vanishes, then R squared plus norm(z-c) squared differs from one. Nonzero projected normals use affine-section avoidance; zero normals have a nonzero constant equation. Collision exclusions are encoded by inner products, with the center c excluded directly by the positive radius. All the finite families may be empty. This proves a geometric supplier; it does not assert a graph-realization or a restoration theorem.
+
+## References
+
+- Truth anchor: `D5/S3/Geometry/SphereSectionAvoidance.circleArc`
+- Truth anchor: `D5/S3/Geometry/SphereSectionAvoidance.exists_on_affine_sphere_avoiding`
+- Truth anchor: `D5/S3/Geometry/SphereSectionAvoidance.exists_on_sphere_avoiding_sections`

+/- GID: D5/S3/Geometry/CosphericalUnitLocus
+   generality: G
+   mirror-B: D5/B/S3/Geometry/CosphericalUnitLocus
+   mirror-E: none(waiver:evidence-not-specified-by-formal-manifest)
+   anchors: [mathlib/module/Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Projection.FiniteDimensional]
+   utility: none
+   digest: Common unit-distance loci of cospherical anchors are exact orthogonal spheres. -/
+module
+
+public import D5.S3.Geometry.SphereSectionAvoidance
+public import Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.Projection.Submodule
+
+/-! Classical orthogonal decomposition of the common sphere intersection.
+The anchor family is nonempty through its specified base index; repeated
+anchors and all carrier codimensions are allowed. -/
+
+noncomputable section
+public section
+
+open Set Metric
+open scoped InnerProductSpace
+
+namespace D5.S3.Geometry.CosphericalUnitLocus
+
+variable {E : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
+
+private theorem unit_locus_iff {ι : Type*} (x : ι → E) (i₀ : ι)
+    (W : Submodule ℝ E) (c : E) (r : ℝ)
+    (hspan : Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range (fun i => x i - x i₀)) = W)
+    (hmem : ∀ i, x i - c ∈ W) (hc : c ∈ Wᗮ) (hx : ∀ i, ‖x i‖ = r)
+    (p : E) :
+    (∀ i, dist p (x i) = 1) ↔
+      p - c ∈ Wᗮ ∧ ‖p - c‖ ^ 2 = 1 - r ^ 2 + ‖c‖ ^ 2 := by
+  have hdistance (hp : p ∈ Wᗮ) (i : ι) :
+      dist p (x i) ^ 2 = ‖p - c‖ ^ 2 + r ^ 2 - ‖c‖ ^ 2 := by
+    have hh := Submodule.inner_left_of_mem_orthogonal (hmem i) hp
+    rw [inner_sub_right] at hh
+    simp only [dist_eq_norm, norm_sub_sq_real, hx i]
+    linarith
+  constructor
+  · intro h
+    have hinner (i : ι) : ⟪p, x i - x i₀⟫_ℝ = 0 := by
+      have hi := congrArg (fun t : ℝ => t ^ 2) (h i)
+      have h0 := congrArg (fun t : ℝ => t ^ 2) (h i₀)
+      simp only [dist_eq_norm, norm_sub_sq_real, hx] at hi h0
+      rw [inner_sub_right]
+      linarith
+    have hker : W ≤ LinearMap.ker (innerSL ℝ p).toLinearMap := by
+      rw [← hspan]
+      refine Submodule.span_le.mpr ?_
+      rintro _ ⟨i, rfl⟩
+      exact hinner i
+    have hp : p ∈ Wᗮ := (W.mem_orthogonal' p).mpr (fun w hw => hker hw)
+    refine ⟨Wᗮ.sub_mem hp hc, ?_⟩
+    have hh := hdistance hp i₀
+    rw [h i₀] at hh
+    linarith
+  · rintro ⟨hpc, hnorm⟩ i
+    have hp : p ∈ Wᗮ := by simpa using Wᗮ.add_mem hpc hc
+    have hh := hdistance hp i
+    nlinarith [dist_nonneg (x := p) (y := x i)]
+
+/-- The direction of the affine hull of the anchor family. -/
+def anchorDirection {ι : Type*} (x : ι → E) (i₀ : ι) : Submodule ℝ E :=
+  Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range (fun i => x i - x i₀))
+
+/-- The nearest-to-zero point of the anchor affine hull, constructed by
+orthogonal projection of its chosen base point. -/
+def anchorCenter [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] {ι : Type*} (x : ι → E) (i₀ : ι) : E :=
+  x i₀ - (anchorDirection x i₀).starProjection (x i₀)
+
+private theorem anchorCenter_mem_orthogonal [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
+    {ι : Type*} (x : ι → E) (i₀ : ι) :
+    anchorCenter x i₀ ∈ (anchorDirection x i₀)ᗮ := by
+  exact (anchorDirection x i₀).sub_starProjection_mem_orthogonal (x i₀)
+
+private theorem sub_anchorCenter_mem [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
+    {ι : Type*} (x : ι → E) (i₀ i : ι) :
+    x i - anchorCenter x i₀ ∈ anchorDirection x i₀ := by
+  have h₁ : x i - x i₀ ∈ anchorDirection x i₀ :=
+    Submodule.subset_span (Set.mem_range_self i)
+  have h₂ : (anchorDirection x i₀).starProjection (x i₀) ∈ anchorDirection x i₀ := by
+    rw [Submodule.starProjection_apply]
+    exact Subtype.coe_prop _
+  convert (anchorDirection x i₀).add_mem h₁ h₂ using 1
+  dsimp [anchorCenter]
+  abel
+
+/-- The exact common-unit locus, with its center and carrier constructed
+from the anchors themselves. This includes codimension-one two-point loci;
+it asserts neither positive dimension nor the existence of a point. -/
+theorem common_unit_locus_iff [FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
+    {ι : Type*} (x : ι → E) (i₀ : ι) (r : ℝ) (hx : ∀ i, ‖x i‖ = r) (p : E) :
+    (∀ i, dist p (x i) = 1) ↔
+      p - anchorCenter x i₀ ∈ (anchorDirection x i₀)ᗮ ∧
+        ‖p - anchorCenter x i₀‖ ^ 2 = 1 - r ^ 2 + ‖anchorCenter x i₀‖ ^ 2 :=
+  unit_locus_iff x i₀ (anchorDirection x i₀) (anchorCenter x i₀) r rfl
+    (sub_anchorCenter_mem x i₀) (anchorCenter_mem_orthogonal x i₀) hx p
+
+/-- Every nonempty open patch of a positive-dimensional common-unit locus
+admits simultaneous avoidance of finitely many forbidden unit distances and

+    rcases i with i | j
+    · intro hi hb
+      apply hproper i hi
+      change (R ^ 2 + ‖z i - c‖ ^ 2 - 1) / 2 = 0 at hb
+      linarith
+    · intro _ hb
+      apply j.property
+      have hq : ‖q j.val - c‖ = 0 := by
+        change ‖q j.val - c‖ ^ 2 = 0 at hb
+        nlinarith [norm_nonneg (q j.val - c)]
+      exact sub_eq_zero.mp (norm_eq_zero.mp hq)
+  have hcont : Continuous (fun w : K => c + (w : E)) :=
+    continuous_const.add continuous_subtype_val
+  obtain ⟨w, hwU, hwR, hw⟩ := exists_on_sphere_avoiding_proper_sections hd hR
+    (hU.preimage hcont) hpatch a b hnormal
+  have hproj (v : E) : ⟪K.orthogonalProjectionOnto v, w⟫_ℝ = ⟪v, (w : E)⟫_ℝ := by
+    exact Submodule.inner_orthogonalProjectionOnto_eq_of_mem_right w v
+  refine ⟨w, hwU, hwR, fun i hi => hw (.inl i) ?_, fun j hj => ?_⟩
+  · change ⟪K.orthogonalProjectionOnto (z i - c), w⟫_ℝ =
+      (R ^ 2 + ‖z i - c‖ ^ 2 - 1) / 2
+    rw [hproj]
+    have hdist : dist (c + (w : E)) (z i) ^ 2 =
+        ‖w‖ ^ 2 - 2 * ⟪z i - c, (w : E)⟫_ℝ + ‖z i - c‖ ^ 2 := by
+      rw [dist_eq_norm]
+      have heq : c + (w : E) - z i = (w : E) - (z i - c) := by abel
+      rw [heq, norm_sub_sq_real, real_inner_comm]
+      rfl
+    rw [hi, hwR] at hdist
+    linarith
+  · by_cases hjc : q j = c
+    · have hw0 : w = 0 := by simpa [hjc] using hj
+      have : ‖w‖ = 0 := by simp [hw0]
+      linarith
+    · apply hw (.inr ⟨j, hjc⟩)
+      change ⟪K.orthogonalProjectionOnto (q j - c), w⟫_ℝ = ‖q j - c‖ ^ 2
+      rw [hproj]
+      have hwq : (w : E) = q j - c := by rw [← hj]; abel
+      rw [hwq, real_inner_self_eq_norm_sq]
+
+end D5.S3.Geometry.SphereSectionAvoidance
